components.text: Whether an inferred intelligence is intelligible and specific enough to support further theistic conclusions.
Whether moral and aesthetic analogies can identify a personal God without relying on contested revelation.
Whether observed cosmic features can support an intelligible intelligence or God hypothesis rather than an incomprehensible referent.
Whether meaningful personal-God descriptions depend on contested scriptural authority.
Whether moral intuition consistently supports a good personal God when Christian scripture is also evaluated by that intuition.
Whether moral intuition consistently supports a good personal God when Christian scripture also conflicts with that intuition.
Whether narrow life-permitting ranges are more expected under an unconstrained creator than under rival explanations.
Whether narrow physical ranges are more expected under an unconstrained creator who seeks thought-permitting life.
Whether fine-tuning comparatively favors the intended creator rather than materially different creator hypotheses.
Whether cosmic order supports only generic intelligence or a morally and religiously specific source.
Whether fine-tuning distinctly favors the intended Christian creator over materially compatible rival creator hypotheses.
Whether the total natural evidence, not fine-tuning alone, is more expected under theism than under atheism.
Whether total cosmic evidence, including lifelessness and evolutionary suffering, favors a loving creator over mindless development.
Whether evolutionary suffering is less expected under a purposeful creator than under mindless natural development.
Whether evolutionary suffering is incompatible with purposeful creation or can accompany an ordered process aimed at complex life.
Whether unknown divine purposes and lawful elegance justify the severe forms of evolutionary suffering actually observed.
Whether appeals to presently unknown explanations are permitted symmetrically for naturalistic fine-tuning accounts.
Whether unknown divine purposes and lawful process adequately answer apparently avoidable evolutionary suffering.
Whether appeals to unknown explanation are applied symmetrically to natural fine-tuning explanations.
Whether natural harms can be avoided while retaining stable laws without continuous divine intervention.
Whether innocent animal and human suffering remains a defeater for a loving creator.
Whether natural harm is avoidable without continual divine intervention into stable physical laws.
Whether a loving creator could permit natural harms for the advent of relational creatures.
Whether skeptical assessment of Christian texts can be separated from prior commitments about their credibility.
Whether skeptical treatment of unique scriptural testimony may be driven by prior commitments rather than the testimony's actual credibility.
Whether Gospel appearance reports are independent historical evidence rather than progressively elaborated later tradition.
Whether later and uniquely attested details merit skepticism for source-critical reasons beyond generic prior commitments.
Whether increasingly elaborate later appearance narratives are independent historical support or evidence of legendary development.
Whether source chronology and narrative elaboration provide evidence beyond a generic appeal to skeptical priors.
Whether identified bodily eyewitnesses maintained resurrection testimony under martyrdom and thereby strengthen the miracle inference.
Whether early testimony independently establishes the principal bodily resurrection facts despite source limitations.
Whether established martyrdom and bodily eyewitness evidence support resurrection rather than uncertain tradition and visionary experience.
Whether early creedal testimony supplies all the claimed resurrection facts despite limitations of Paul's evidence.
Whether limitations in particular resurrection evidence defeat a broader cumulative route to Christian faith.
Whether source-development concerns overturn the cumulative Christian identification rather than limiting one component.
Whether moral orientation remains affirmative evidence despite scriptural moral tensions.
Whether limited human comprehension warrants agnosticism about God or merely undercuts confident denial while cumulative evidence remains available.
Whether moral orientation and Jesus's teaching can remain parts of a cumulative Christian case.
Whether resurrection evidence survives source-development objections strongly enough for Christian identification.
Whether a striking private experience can justify belief and what evidential force it has for people who lack access to it.
Whether a striking private revelation can justify its recipient while remaining inaccessible as public evidence to others.
Whether a specific transformative prayer experience has an external divine source or transferable evidential force.
Whether beauty positively supports a personal good God rather than merely producing intense or unsettled affect.
Whether numinous affect constitutes publicly discriminating revelation.
Whether natural, neural, or evolutionary mediation eliminates or substantially weakens the possible divine significance of beauty.
Whether evolved capacities can mediate revelation while leaving its public accessibility and source verification unresolved.
Whether evolutionary or neural explanations exhaust the meaning of beauty and music or leave room for divine significance.
Whether evolved human capacities can mediate revelation accessible through ordinary experience.
